title: Walk through what happens during exactly-once processing end-to-end (transaction coordinator, commit markers, producer ID/epoch fencing).
shortTitle: Walk through what happens during exactly-once processing end-to-end.
keyPoints: Exactly-once is built from three pieces: idempotent writes, Kafka transactions, and producer-id/epoch fencing.
The idempotent producer uses a PID and per-partition sequence numbers so the broker drops retry duplicates.
Transactions atomically commit output records and consumed offsets together under a stable transactional.id.
The transaction coordinator manages transactional state in an internal transaction log topic.
Commit markers (control records) are written to every partition the transaction touched, telling consumers which records are committed.
Epoch fencing disables zombie producers: initTransactions() bumps the epoch so old instances are rejected.
Consumers must use isolation.level=read_committed to see only committed transaction records.

s1_definition.oneliner: Exactly-once is idempotent writes plus a transaction that atomically commits output records and input offsets together, with a transaction coordinator, commit markers, and producer-id-and-epoch fencing stopping duplicates and zombies.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Idempotent producer** -- uses a broker-assigned producer id (PID) and per-partition sequence numbers to drop retry duplicates.
- **Transaction coordinator** -- a broker-side component that manages transactional state in an internal transaction log topic (`__transaction_state`).
- **transactional.id** -- a stable identifier that survives producer restarts; lets the coordinator track and fence a producer across sessions.
- **Commit markers** -- special control records written to every partition the transaction touched; they tell consumers which records belong to committed transactions.
- **Epoch fencing** -- when a new producer calls `initTransactions()`, the coordinator bumps the epoch for that transactional.id, rejecting any writes from the old (zombie) instance.
- **read_committed** -- consumer isolation level that delivers only committed transaction records and skips aborted or in-flight ones.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine a National Bank of India clerk who moves money and records it in the ledger. Exactly-once is like a notarized atomic operation: either both the money movement and the ledger entry happen, or neither does. If the clerk is replaced mid-task, the old clerk's badge is revoked so he cannot sneak back and do the work twice. A special stamp on the ledger page says this block of entries is officially committed, and readers ignore entries without that stamp.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Exactly-Once Processing End-to-End

  Consumer                  Producer (tx.id)           Coordinator
  ┌────────┐               ┌────────────────┐         ┌──────────────┐
  │ poll() │               │ initTransactions│────────▶│ Assign epoch │
  │        │               │ begin()        │         │ epoch=2      │
  │ records│──process──────▶│ send(settle-0) │         │              │
  │        │               │ send(settle-3) │         │ Track parts  │
  │ offsets│──────────────▶│ sendOffsets()  │         │              │
  │        │               │ commit()       │────────▶│ PREPARE      │
  └────────┘               └────────────────┘         │ Write COMMIT │
                                                      │ markers to:  │
                                                      │  settle-0    │
                                                      │  settle-3    │
                                                      │  __offsets   │
                                                      │ COMMITTED    │
                                                      └──────────────┘

  Zombie (epoch=1):
  ┌──────────────────┐         ┌──────────────┐
  │ Old producer     │──send──▶│ Coordinator  │
  │ epoch=1          │         │ epoch=1 < 2  │
  │                  │◀─REJECT─│ FENCED!      │
  └──────────────────┘         └──────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Exactly-once processing in Kafka is built from three pieces. The idempotent producer uses a PID and sequence numbers so the broker drops retry duplicates. Transactions wrap output records and consumed offsets in one atomic commit managed by the transaction coordinator, which writes commit markers to every partition the transaction touched. Epoch fencing ensures a zombie producer cannot sneak back and commit stale work.

On the reading side, consumers set isolation level to read_committed so they only see committed records and skip anything aborted or in-flight. The consume-process-produce loop with sendOffsetsToTransaction is the foundation of exactly-once stream processing.

At National Bank of India, this guaranteed that a transfer was never settled twice even under retries, crashes, or a zombie instance. The important caveat is that exactly-once is end-to-end only inside Kafka. For external systems like the ledger database, Rajesh makes writes idempotent or uses the outbox pattern.

Remember one sentence: exactly-once is idempotent writes plus a transaction that atomically commits output and offsets together, with epoch fencing stopping zombies and commit markers telling consumers which records are real.
